sub_scenario.one_line: platform operations coordinator: poor fit as currently run

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the runbook index and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The service inventory review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I took the 07:00 routine status readout this week and it went smoothly.
So early itself is not a problem?
Not when I am reading from a prepared sheet.
Someone new shadowed me in the operations bay this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the incident handoffs into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
During the payments outage I sketched the service dependency map from the handoff notes before the review call, and the restore order came out right: storage first, then the API tier.
The written map came before the live decision?
Yes. Without it I would have been guessing under pressure.
I led a complex restore-sequencing call at noon last month and it went well.
What made it work?
The dependency notes were in front of me before we started.
I archived last cycle's notes on the service inventory and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My alarm has been dragging me up at five for the gym trial, and I have noticed my judgment before eight is slower even when I feel awake.
Does routine work suffer too?
No, reading and filing are fine. It is the weighing of options that lags.
A vendor call about the runbook index ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the operations bay checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the incident handoffs.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the service inventory records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On Tuesday's 06:00 bridge the overnight notes were not posted yet, and I ordered the cache restore ahead of account recovery. Sam had to stop me and resequence it live.
What was missing?
The dependency picture. I could see every alert but not how they chained.
I sketched next week's plan for the incident handoffs before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the runbook index updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I asked the overnight shift to post their handoff summary by 05:30 going forward, but the tooling only publishes at 06:30.
So the notes arrive after the bridge starts.
Exactly, an hour too late.
I compared two options for the service inventory tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the operations bay handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
My manager asked me point blank whether the standing 06:00 incident bridge is a slot where I would do my best work. What should I tell her?
